verdicts.quote: The user finds an entry point in the designated org that opens the bot. … The bot does not automatically include Salesforce record data in Grok input.
verdicts.missing: The Salesforce surface and the context it passes to the bot are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: The bot does not automatically include Salesforce record data in Grok input. … access to existing objects, fields, records, and unrelated apps is the same after bot setup as before it.
verdicts.missing: Setup preserves record access, but the spec gives no requirement to run record reads in the asking user's sharing context.

verdicts.quote: For each affected user, access to existing objects, fields, records, and unrelated apps is the same after bot setup as before it.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say how field-level permissions, encryption or restrictions govern the bot's reads and displayed answers.

verdicts.quote: A signed-in user without bot authorization cannot invoke Grok through the bot … An operator with the applicable setup authority can install a valid credential
verdicts.missing: The Salesforce permission set or equivalent entitlement for bot users and for administrators is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: each sees only their own result … the earlier interaction is not available as a saved transcript in Salesforce.
verdicts.missing: Concurrent replies are isolated and there is no saved Salesforce transcript. Administrator access to conversations is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: the external service used in U-2 may fail to return a complete result
verdicts.missing: The spec does not require an asynchronous Salesforce callout or define how it is scheduled outside a trigger or transaction with preceding DML.

verdicts.quote: Inspecting the bot page, its browser requests, and its user-visible errors does not expose the configured credential.
verdicts.missing: The protected storage mechanism and the exclusion of secrets from source code, metadata and logs are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: They see that the prompt is pending if the answer is still being generated. When Grok answers, they read its reply within Salesforce.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say how the interface detects completion and retrieves or receives the reply.

verdicts.quote: After interruption, reopening the bot generates zero new Grok requests for the interrupted submission by itself.
verdicts.missing: The spec prevents replay on reopen but does not define how duplicate reply posting is prevented when an async job runs again.

verdicts.quote: the operator can identify the provider access problem … the user sees a service failure for the submission. … the user sees that the submission timed out.
verdicts.missing: Server errors and timeouts have distinct user outcomes. Recognized 401 and 403 rejections have an operator diagnosis but no specified user-visible outcome.

verdicts.quote: The user sees the relevant problem. They can submit again after capacity returns or the operator restores the allowance.
verdicts.missing: The spec allows manual resubmission but does not say whether the bot retries automatically or what backoff or retry limit applies.

verdicts.quote: If the bot displays text from an incomplete response, the user can tell the displayed reply is incomplete. … If no terminal result arrives by the active deadline, the user sees that the submission timed out.
The bot does not create saved Salesforce conversation history.
verdicts.missing: The spec rules out saved Salesforce history and supplies no conversation or turn record schema with roles, text, status, timestamps, model and usage.

verdicts.quote: After a user closes the bot and opens it again, the earlier interaction is not available as a saved transcript in Salesforce.
verdicts.missing: The spec defines what is available after reopening, but does not define deletion of conversation data, including when a user is deleted.

verdicts.quote: With an existing record open in Salesforce, submitting text that omits the record's data sends none of that record's fields or attachments to Grok.
verdicts.missing: Automatic record context is excluded. The spec gives no visibility or personal-data rule for org data a user includes in the prompt.

verdicts.quote: When Grok rejects the request for excessive input length, the user sees that the prompt needs to be shortened.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say whether previous turns are included, or when and how an oversized conversation is trimmed or summarised.

verdicts.quote: opens the bot for the first time … A submission containing zero characters or only whitespace receives input feedback and generates zero Grok requests. … measured at the exact published maximum proceeds past the bot's length validation.
The operator can revoke a user's bot access. … The operator can determine the exact model identifier in use for the development org. … the operator can identify the provider access problem.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not give an administrator an org-wide off switch, a model-change operation or a way to inspect failed requests generally.

verdicts.quote: If the destination is missing, ambiguous, or a production business org, deployment stops before changes are made.
verdicts.missing: The org type and deployment method, environment-specific configuration and credentials, and production code-coverage requirement are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: The deployed bot or its operating instructions give the exact positive deadline in seconds, measured from acceptance of the submission. … While an accepted submission is awaiting its result, the user can tell that processing is in progress.
verdicts.missing: The builder must choose the actual latency bound. The spec gives its unit and starting point and requires pending feedback.

verdicts.quote: The bot indicates that it needs a text prompt. … the user can tell that processing is in progress. … the user sees that the request failed. … the user sees an outcome identifying the request as declined.
verdicts.missing: The initial empty view and the presentation of these states are unspecified beyond the feedback each must communicate.

verdicts.quote: access to existing objects, fields, records, and unrelated apps is the same … deployment has not created, altered, or deleted those records. … An existing workflow or automation outside the bot still produces its prior observable result
